newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end up on technicals, Dow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end up on technicals, Dow.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished up again on Monday, with the December Standard & Poor's 500 stock index contract chalking up another all-time high on a wave of institutional buying.
"It just seems like everyone wants to own this thing. It's kind of evident over the last six months," said a trader in the S&P 500s pit.

On the day, December S&Ps pushed through several technical resistance levels to make a new contract high in the past half-hour of trading at 760.60. "The buying continues. The institutionals are strong all around," a trader said.
The previous December S&P 500s high was 751.80 set Friday.
Fueling the rally was a powerful rise in the Dow Jones industrial average, up 76.03 to 6,547.79, one trader said.

Stock index futures got an early lift from bonds, which rose early on a report from the National Association of Realtors that sales of existing U.S. homes fell 1.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.97 million units from a revised 4.03 million units in September.
Bonds lost their momentum at midday, but stock futures continued a steady rise. "Basically right now it's a momentum market," said one technical analyst.

At the end of pit trading, December S&P 500s were up 8.75 points to 759.95, KBT Value Lines were up 6.80 points to 685.00, Nikkeis were up 160.0 at 21,420.0, Midcap 400s were up 1.20 at 257.00 and Nasdaq 100s were up 3.25 at 825.75. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
